# DropSpace v0.2.0-preview.3

This is an experimental Preview hotfix for DropSpace's **smart file-drag wake** architecture. It does not replace v0.1.0 Stable for important work.

Official website: https://dropspace.pages.dev/

## Smart wake signal repair

- Fixes the remaining no-response path in Smart mode. Preview.2 still made one asynchronous UI Automation item hit-test the effective gate; when Explorer entered its OLE drag loop, that inspection could resolve to `Unknown`, mouse observation stopped, and later drag events tried to classify the cursor after it had already left the source item.
- Adds two independent documented Windows accessibility signal ranges: `EVENT_OBJECT_DRAGSTART/CANCEL/COMPLETE` and provider-supplied `EVENT_SYSTEM_DRAGDROPSTART/END`. The WinEvent callback only enqueues non-content metadata and never blocks or modifies input.
- Removes the deprecated root-wide `UiaAddEvent` startup dependency that could prevent the observer thread from reaching its message pump. Bounded UI Automation and MSAA file-item hit-testing remain as source evidence.
- Separates “press occurred in a known Explorer/Desktop file-view surface” from “UI Automation identified the exact item.” A documented drag-start event can promote the verified Shell surface even when the item leaf is transiently unavailable. The mouse-threshold-only fallback still requires exact item evidence.
- Final acceptance is unchanged: the temporary visible OLE target must receive a real `CF_HDROP`; invalid or virtual-only data returns `DROPEFFECT_NONE`, and source files are never moved or deleted.
- Portable smoke now requires both the observation-only mouse hook and the documented object-drag event hook to be registered in Smart mode.

## One placement coordinate system

- Fixes the state-specific offset that moved only DragApproaching/DragReady below Windows Drop Tray, then sprang Compact, Expanded, Dismissing, or Notch back to the screen edge.
- Smart mode now uses one DPI-aware physical offset for every visual lifecycle state and for both Dynamic Island and Notch. Drop feedback, completed-drop Compact state, Expanded state, mode transitions, full-screen dismissal, and reverse animations share that anchor.
- Enlarges the transparent fixed host to contain the full offset Expanded surface at 100%, 125%, 150%, 175%, and 200% DPI. The shaped HRGN remains limited to visible pixels, so the extra transparent host area does not become an input target.

## Preview limitations

- GitHub Actions validates hook registration, state policy, target geometry, synthetic `CF_HDROP`, DPI containment, installer lifecycle, Portable and MSIX builds. It cannot prove that every Windows 11 Explorer/Desktop build raises the same cross-process accessibility events.
- Real Windows 11 testing is still required for Explorer/Desktop left- and right-button drags, fast cancellation, Drop Tray coexistence, multi-monitor placement, Dynamic Island/Notch visual alignment, and false-positive behavior.
- Some third-party applications and virtual-file providers may not expose enough public evidence. Use **Traditional top-edge zone (compatibility mode)** when needed.
- This Preview is unsigned. Unattended automatic installation remains disabled; verified updates require explicit user action.

Stable-channel users will not receive this Preview. Select the Preview channel only to test experimental builds.
